steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Combine 1 1/4 cup cookie crumbs, 1/4 cup sugar, and 1/4 cup butter; press into a 9-inch pie plate. Bake in preheated oven for 10 minutes. Cool on wire rack.
In a mixing bowl, beat cream cheese, peanut butter, 1 cup sugar, 1 tablespoon butter, and vanilla until smooth. Whip the cream, and fold into the peanut butter mixture.
Gently spoon filing into crust. Garnish pie with chocolate or cookie crumbs if desired. Refrigerate for several hours before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Peanut Butter Pie I
raw_recipe.description: This pie has a chocolate crumb crust and a creamy peanut butter filling. Garnish pie with grated chocolate or chocolate cookie crumbs, if desired.
raw_recipe.name: Peanut Butter Pie I

review.reviewBody: I needed a quick dessert for an impromptu dinner and decided to try this recipe. It was absolutely delicious and a big hit. I did make a few minor adjustments based on feedback from a friend of mine who made it. I cheated and used a Keebler chocolate crumb crust (something I rarely do but was pressed for time). I decreased the sugar to 3/4 c and increased the whipping cream to 1.5 c to make it a little fluffier. I also popped it in the freezer for a few hours before serving. Wow!!! I'll certainly be making this again and again and again....well, you get the picture! :-)

Made this with a Gluten Free crust ( chocolate cream filled cookies ground with butter and sugar as the recipe directs)
Used my Pampered Chef Whip Cream Maker to whip the heavy whipping cream since I had already used my Kitchen Aid to beat the peanut butter and cream cheese. This was the best plan! Worked great! turned out amazing! Had to adjust the baking of the crust a bit though

I used the crust recipe I have for ice cream pie, which is 24 cookies, crushed & 1/4 c unsalted butter - cook for 15 minutes @ 350. I also followed another reviewers advice to reduce sugar and increase heavy cream to make the filling fluffier. The pie turned out VERY good and I received multiple compliments on it from co-workers; however, my personal opinion is the pie tasted a bit too buttery. even though there's only 1 Tbsp of butter. Not sure what would cause this, but due to amazing taste anyway - I gave the pie 4 stars.

This is excellent! Disclaimer first: I make pies quite often, so I'm duly savvy as to ingredients and proportions. My first instinct to limit the sugar in the filling by 50% was solid! On another note, I was frustrated in shopping for chocolate cookies and wasn't willing to strip Oreos of their filling, so I opted for graham crackers, which I granulated with a rolling pin, largely creating sand, but that sand was wonderfully married by the butter and sugar, so worries were soon aborted. As to peanut butter, I used a blue label brand, the reigning assumption being a high sugar content, one reason for the sugar diminution. I added cocoa powder, two tablespoons, in hopes to compensate for the chocolate-less crust . Finally, I grated unsweetened chocolate over the top, snowfall effect, mainly for appearance but also to balance sweetness. My pre-bite reflection was that recipe lends itself to variation/tampering as crust, filling, and topping can be played with not just to please personal tastes but also aesthetics. My post-bit reflection: Heaven (or devilshly decadent)! A caveat to close with... this is a dessert pie, which you might think redundant phrasing, but the heavy cream, strong flavor, and density should cue people to my point. (To be clear, a no-sugar-added Granny Smith apple pie might occupy the opposite end of the spectrum.)

I've been making this recipe for years! It's my favorite peanut butter pie recipe and I always have requests for this. I buy a pre-made oreo crust to save time. I also garnish the pie with freshly grated chocolate and small slices of peanut butter cups. I recently discovered how to make this as bite sizes since it's so rich (less guilt). For mini's, I sprinkle ground up oreo's into the bottom of a mini muffin pan liners (placed on a cookie sheet), I then put the filling into a pastry bag or plastic bag with a whole cut out and I fill each cup with the filling, garnish and chill. The filling will stick to the crust when you take it out. Keep it refrigerated until it's ready to be served. If you have larger mini muffin liners you could use one side of an oreo with the frosting scraped off and it would hold together even better.

I made this gluten free and chocolate free due to allergies. Instead of the cookie crums I take a cup of peacons ground up in a food processor. Then I bake the crust for about 10 minutes at 350. I also don't fold the heavy cream. I put all the ingredients in and mix it up until it's fluffy and fully mixed well.. its so good.
It’s great, I use crunchy peanut butter and for a crust I used brownie batter pre-baked and frozen in a spring form pan. I also serve it frozen.

5 stars with the changes I made! The crust does not need any added sugar at all. The cookie crumbs are sweet enough. On the pie filling, omit butter and use powdered sugar instead of granulated. I had some peanut butter chips and melted about 1/2 cup mixed wit some heavy whipping cream to make a ganache. I spread a layer of that in the bottom of the crust before adding the filling. I also made some homemade chocolate sauce to garnish. No wonder I didn't need added sugar in the crust with all of that. Also topped with fresh whipped cream and chopped peanuts. Yep ***** 5 STARS!!

I made mini versions of these for a potluck and they disappeared in minutes. I made a double recipe of the cookie crust and pressed it into non-stick mini muffin tins, then baked at 350 for 7 min (made about 35). My mini crusts popped right out after cooling for a few minutes. I then made 1 1/2 times the recipe of filling and used a piping tip in a ziploc bag to pipe filling into each shell. I finished by sprinkling each mini pie with mini chocolate chips. I ended up with a LOT of filling left over and no energy to make more crust, so I took a few leftover chocolate wafers and set them in regular size muffin tins, filled with remaining topping and stuck in the freezer - those turned out fabulous, too and we are still eating them. I like a really dense and peanut-buttery pie, so when I make these again, I'll try using 2/3rds to 1/2 the amount of whipped cream and maybe a little less sugar. So yummy and so simple! Thanks Stephanie!

Amazing, rich, and creamy! I skipped the crumb crust just because I don't care for it and used a regular pastry crust instead. I put down about half a cup of chocolate chips when the crust came out of the oven and let them melt to spread around to kind of make up for the lack of chocolate from the crumb crust. This pie was excellent the day I made it but I honestly think it was even better the next day. When I make this again I'm going to make it a day ahead. Thanks for the great submission.

I made the crust with pb oreos. I also added a thin layer of melted pb kisses to the bottom of the crust b4 adding the filling. I added an egg & sour cream & baked this pie. It was a hit. I took it 2 a friend's house & everyone really enjoyed it. Even with the added sweetness I didn't over do it. I will definitely be making this again
Turned out great! I used extra crunchy peanut butter too. Sprinkled the top with chocolate shavings as well.
I came across this recipe, because I was looking for something quick and easy. I have so many people asking me to make it again. I made one change, honey roasted peanut butter! You won't be sorry
This is a very easy recipe and my whole family loves it!!
Recipe was fairly simple and final product was delicious! I used oreo's for the crust, and even used the Oreo filling to make a buttercream icing for it. I would recommend this recipe!

I used a premade shell since I already had it. half the cream cheese because it's what I had and half the sugar. It's still so sweet and realllyy delicious. I didn't bake it because I didn't make my shell so it's sitting in the fridge.

Super easy and delicious! I followed another reviewers advice to decrease the sugar to 3/4 cup and it was perfect. I also used a Keebler chocolate pie crust and crunchy peanut butter. Making it again tomorrow; it was so good 😊
Great peanut butter pie. Very easy to make. Very easy to make gluten free. I used gluten free cookies (Oreo style) to make the crust and it turned out great.

It was wonderful, out wasn't as peanut buttery as we like so I did add 1/3c more peanut butter . Either way this was delicious . FYI make sure u allow the hour to set in fridge! My family didn't want to wait and the next day they saw the difference. I'm gonna to one tomorrow same rebuild but with the graham cracker mix bc the already made was so hard. Over all 💚
